<!--
  This is not the bug form. Nothing here is broken — it looks wrong, or it costs
  more moves than it should. Both are worth opening, and both are judged the same
  way: by looking and by using, not by a passing test.
-->

## Where

<!-- The screen and the state, both. "The composer" is not enough: grid or focus,
     folded or raised, idle or working, first launch or restored. Most of these only
     appear in one combination. -->

## What you were trying to do

<!-- The task, not the interaction. "Open the next changed file" rather than "click
     the tree". Skip this if it is purely about how something looks. -->

## What happens now

<!--
  A screenshot if it is about looks. If it is about friction, the moves instead —
  the whole loop, including the parts that feel like nothing: "click a file, the
  tree disappears, press escape, click the next one." That sentence is the issue.
-->

## What is wrong about it

<!--
  Say what it reads as, or what it costs you. "The panel looks like it has a hole
  in the bottom" leads somewhere; "make it darker" is already an answer to a
  question nobody asked yet. For friction: the moves you repeat, what you have to
  keep in your head, what goes away that you still needed.
-->

## What it should do instead

<!-- The intent. "The card should look like it can be pulled up", "the tree should
     survive opening a file" — rather than a radius value or a layout. -->

## Measured

<!--
  Optional, and worth more than any adjective. Colours, pixel distances, the two
  values you compared. Clicks, seconds, round trips. Arguments about contrast end
  the moment someone posts the two hex values, and can run for days without them.
-->
